title: High-Dimension Human Value Representation in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark, UniVaR, measures the representation of high-dimensional human values in Large Language Models. This includes culturally specific values derived from religious and philosophical traditions, such as Islamic, Hindu, Confucian, and Buddhist value systems, by analyzing LLM responses to value-eliciting questions across various languages.
findings: The paper found that LLMs' value representations cluster by language, and these clusters often align with real-world cultural-religious groupings. For instance, models prompted in languages from predominantly Islamic cultures (Indonesian, Malaysian, Arabic) clustered together, while those prompted in East Asian languages (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) formed another cluster reflecting shared Confucian and Buddhist values. This indicates that LLMs embed and represent distinct, religiously-influenced cultural value systems based on their training data and prompting language.
references: Aakanksha, Arash Ahmadian, Beyza Ermis, Seraphina Goldfarb-Tarrant, Julia Kreutzer, Marzieh Fadaee, and Sara Hooker. 2024. The multilingual alignment prism: Aligning global and local preferences to reduce harm. Preprint, arXiv:2406.18682.
